advisories.title: PostgreSQL extension script schema mishandling executes arbitrary SQL
advisories.summary: Uncontrolled search path element in PostgreSQL CREATE EXTENSION allows an attacker with database-level CREATE privilege to execute arbitrary code as the bootstrap superuser, via ALTER SCHEMA ... RENAME or CREATE EXTENSION ... SCHEMA "$user".  ALTER EXTENSION was also affected.  A trusted-extension script located the wrong object and executed arbitrary SQL of the attacker's choice.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL type confusion after ALTER ... SET DATA TYPE executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Type confusion in PostgreSQL allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via ALTER ... SET DATA TYPE primarily.  Other DDL attack routes exist, such as "ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN; ROLLBACK; ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN".  The system had inadequate tracking of typed values, and values were not self-identifying.  Stale values could appear in data dictionary entries, PL/pgSQL variables, and many other parts of the system.  PostgreSQL Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL output parameter type confusion executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Type confusion in PostgreSQL SQL-language functions allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via an output parameter of type "any".  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL pg_basebackup can use backup manifest content as a format string
advisories.summary: Use of externally-controlled format string in PostgreSQL pg_basebackup allows an attacker having already compromised a server to achieve disclosure from pg_basebackup memory, via backup manifest bytes.  The vulnerability does not return the improperly-read bytes back to the attacker's server, so a successful attack would need separate implementation-specific secrets for that.  Integrity impact is unlikely; in particular, the applicable formatter does not support %n.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT can read or modify rows despite auto-updatable view WHERE condition
advisories.summary: Improper protection in PostgreSQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT on auto-updatable views allows an attacker having INSERT and UPDATE privileges on the view to read and modify every row in the view's base table, via iterated INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE.  This bypasses the view's WHERE condition, whether or not the view is a security_barrier view.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL dblink and subscriptions can append to arbitrary files
advisories.summary: External control of file name in PostgreSQL dblink and CREATE/ALTER SUBSCRIPTION allows a user to achieve persistent denial of service, via appending invalid data to a chosen file.  Specifically, the "sslkeylogfile" connection parameter appends data, in NSS keylog format, to a file of the user's choosing.  This "sslkeylogfile" mechanism cannot add arbitrary bytes.  Within major version 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18 are also affected if libpq version 18 or later is installed and in use by the server.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT can read rows despite row security policies
advisories.summary: Improper protection in PostgreSQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT allows an attacker having INSERT, UPDATE, and applicable SELECT privileges on the table to read every row despite row security policies, via iterated INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE.  Unlike CVE-2026-16237, this does not facilitate improper writes.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL extension-script substitutions allow SQL injection through object names
advisories.summary: SQL injection in PostgreSQL extension-script substitutions allows an attacker with database-level CREATE privilege to execute arbitrary code as the bootstrap superuser, via a schema or owner name containing newlines or other special substrings.  This is similar to CVE-2023-39417, but it requires a non-bundled extension with a vulnerable script pattern.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL pg_show_all_settings() use-after-free discloses memory
advisories.summary: Use after free in PostgreSQL pg_show_all_settings() allows a database user to retrieve memory contents, via loading a module while the function is scanning custom-variable placeholders that the module replaces and frees.  Within major versions 16-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, and 16.16 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 16 are unaffected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL plpgsql record-field type confusion executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Type confusion in PostgreSQL plpgsql record-field assignment allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via a reentrant domain CHECK that changes a RECORD variable's row type while a value is being cast.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL expanded-record domain-check use-after-free executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Use after free in PostgreSQL expanded-record domain checks allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via repeated checks of a domain over a composite type that cause reuse of a dangling memory-context pointer.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL FDW batch-insert mismatch executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Heap-based buffer overflow in PostgreSQL foreign batch inserts allows a foreign server to execute arbitrary code, via reporting that it inserted more rows than the server supplied.  postgres_fdw can legitimately encounter this when a rule on the remote table expands an INSERT into additional rows.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL extended-statistics pseudo-type confusion executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Type confusion in PostgreSQL extended statistics allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via a statistics expression of an anonymous RECORD type whose backend-local type identifier denotes a different row type in another session.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL dblink reentrant disconnect use-after-free executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Use after free in the PostgreSQL dblink extension allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via type conversion code that re-enters dblink and closes a connection whose results an outer dblink call is reading.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL REASSIGN OWNED bypasses role SET and CREATEDB checks
advisories.summary: Missing authorization in PostgreSQL REASSIGN OWNED allows a role granted INHERIT but not SET to transfer objects to the granted role.  It also allows reassignment of database ownership without the CREATEDB privilege.  The equivalent ALTER ... OWNER commands block this.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL logical replication can write to subscriber system catalogs, executing arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Missing authorization in PostgreSQL logical replication allows a compromised publisher to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the superuser-owned subscription, via naming a system catalog as a replication target.  Only subscriptions owned by a superuser are vulnerable.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL type-cache invalidation gap executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Type confusion from incomplete PostgreSQL type-cache invalidation allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via a composite type change while its cache entry is being populated.  Within major version 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL transition-table cursor use-after-free executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Use after free in PostgreSQL trigger functions allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via a cursor over a transition table.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL dropped-column type confusion executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Type confusion in PostgreSQL anonymous RECORD types allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via row types having dropped attributes in the same positions but with different widths or alignments.  Within major versions 17-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 and 17.12 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 17 are unaffected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL materialized set-returning function type confusion executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Type confusion in PostgreSQL materialized set-returning functions allows a database user to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via returning rows having different dynamic RECORD return types.  json_populate_recordset() is one affected function.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL tuple-size integer wraparound executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Integer wraparound in PostgreSQL in-memory tuple-size calculations allows a database user to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via oversized tuple data.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL REINDEX CONCURRENTLY does not block DROP INDEX during index functions
advisories.summary: Operation on a dropped index in PostgreSQL REINDEX CONCURRENTLY allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via an index expression that issues DROP INDEX.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL commutator or negator result-type confusion executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Type confusion in PostgreSQL operator commutator and negator links allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via linking operators having different result types or creating inconsistent reciprocal links.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL parallel B-tree array scan reads beyond array bounds
advisories.summary: Buffer over-read in PostgreSQL parallel B-tree scans allows an object creator to read attacker-chosen server-memory addresses, via a function incorrectly marked PARALLEL SAFE or STABLE to make participating workers build different scan-key arrays.  Within major versions 17-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 and 17.12 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 17 are unaffected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL portal setup use-after-free executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Use after free in PostgreSQL portal setup allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via running user-defined code during planning or executor startup that closes the portal currently being prepared.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL min/max aggregate type confusion executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Type confusion in PostgreSQL min/max aggregate optimization allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via a user-defined aggregate whose SORTOP option causes the planner to treat the aggregate's input and result as the same type when they differ.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL pg_dump tar restore.sql fails to block psql command injection
advisories.summary: Untrusted data inclusion in PostgreSQL pg_dump tar-format restore.sql allows a compromised origin server to execute arbitrary code as the client operating system account running psql, via the predictable restriction key in restore.sql.  This is a gap in the fix for CVE-2025-8714.  restore.sql is undocumented.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL statistics import type confusion executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Type confusion in PostgreSQL statistics import allows a table maintainer to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via nested SET DATA TYPE during conversion of values to import.  Within major version 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL generation memory context integer wraparound executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Integer wraparound in PostgreSQL generation memory contexts allows a database user to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via freeing an allocation larger than 1 GB and causing its block to be reused for smaller chunks whose back-pointer offset cannot represent that position.  Within major versions 16-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, and 16.16 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 16 are unaffected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL security_barrier analysis can expose hidden values through indirect expressions
advisories.summary: Exposure of sensitive information in PostgreSQL security_barrier processing allows a database user to infer values hidden by a security_barrier view, via applying a leaky function to a CASE test value or internal parameter that indirectly represents a protected column.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL plperl tied-object exceptions follow stale sigjmp_buf
advisories.summary: Uncaught exceptions in PostgreSQL plperl allow an object creator to cause use of a stale sigjmp_buf, via a tied Perl object, or a Perl object whose overloaded conversion throws while plperl is handling another error.  We have not ruled out arbitrary code execution on some platform.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL reindexdb index name quoting allows SQL injection
advisories.summary: SQL injection in PostgreSQL reindexdb allows an object creator to execute arbitrary SQL as the database user running reindexdb, via a crafted index name embedded in the parallel catalog query for --jobs with --index.  Within major versions 17-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 and 17.12 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 17 are unaffected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL pltcl reentrant result conversion use-after-free executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Use after free in PostgreSQL pltcl allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via a domain CHECK that re-enters the Tcl interpreter and frees or changes a string still used by the outer result conversion.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL pre-authentication cancel request can leak a spinlock
advisories.summary: Improper locking in PostgreSQL startup processing allows an unauthenticated network client to trigger a server restart, via arranging for authentication_timeout to arrive while it holds a spinlock during cancel handling.  Within major version 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL unterminated name value discloses server memory
advisories.summary: Improper null termination in PostgreSQL array element assignment allows a database user to disclose server memory, via changing the final byte of a fixed-length name value to a nonzero byte and passing it to code that treats the value as a C string.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL plperl array and hash conversion use-after-free executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Use after free in PostgreSQL plperl allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via dropping the final reference to a Perl array or hash while PostgreSQL is converting that object.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL plperl reentrant return_next() use-after-free executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Use after free in PostgreSQL plperl allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via reentrant return_next() calls.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL pg_dump not-null constraint name allows SQL injection
advisories.summary: SQL injection in PostgreSQL pg_dump allows an object creator to execute arbitrary SQL as the user restoring the dump, via an inherited column having a child-local not-null constraint whose name requires quoting.  Within major version 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL ts_rank_cd() heap buffer overflow may execute arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Heap-based buffer overflow in PostgreSQL ts_rank_cd() may allow a database user to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via an invalid tsvector containing duplicate positions.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL security-restricted operations can create types in pg_temp, which later queries of the session find
advisories.summary: Improper protection of alternate path in PostgreSQL security-restricted operations allows an object creator to execute arbitrary SQL as the operation's caller, via a domain, enum, or range type created in pg_temp.  The victim session must later run a query containing an unqualified type name, e.g. "SELECT '1'::bigint"; autovacuum and other common security-restricted operation users do not do so, so they are unaffected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL tsvector_delete() heap buffer overflow executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Heap-based buffer overflow in PostgreSQL tsvector_delete() allows a database user to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via a tsvector whose lexeme data uses a nonstandard but valid ordering that requires additional alignment padding in the result.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL pg_restore executes arbitrary code due to missing non-plain archive validation
advisories.summary: Improper input validation in PostgreSQL pg_restore allows a non-plain archive provider to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running pg_restore, via a crafted archive.  Note a contrast: crafted archive data may legitimately cause arbitrary SQL to execute at the restore destination, but it does not legitimately confer arbitrary code execution in the pg_restore OS process.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL "vacuumdb --missing-stats-only" lets a database owner execute code as the vacuumdb user
advisories.summary: Untrusted search path in PostgreSQL vacuumdb allows a database owner to execute arbitrary SQL as the database user running vacuumdb, via shadowing operators used in the --missing-stats-only catalog query.  The pg_upgrade documentation recommends an affected vacuumdb invocation.  Within major version 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL MERGE can place the wrong row in a trigger transition table
advisories.summary: Inconsistent transition-capture state in PostgreSQL MERGE allows a table data modifier to make an AFTER trigger process the wrong new row, via a partitioned table MERGE that performs an INSERT before an UPDATE.  Within major versions 15-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, and 15.20 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 15 are unaffected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL DROP OWNED can remove restrictive row security policies from non-owned tables
advisories.summary: Missing authorization in PostgreSQL DROP OWNED allows a role to remove itself from restrictive row level security policies, thereby reading or modifying rows that the policy was intended to deny, via queries after the DROP OWNED.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL COPY error context uses freed field storage
advisories.summary: Use after free in PostgreSQL COPY FROM error reporting allows a database user to disclose portions of server memory, via a longer input row following an ignored or nullified conversion error.  file_fdw reaches the same code path in affected version 18.  Within major versions 17-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 and 17.12 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 17 are unaffected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL plperl blessed-reference type confusion may execute arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Type confusion in PostgreSQL plperl may allow an object creator to execute arbitrary code, via blessing a non-hash reference into PostgreSQL::InServer::ARRAY.  We have not confirmed or ruled out a way to control the pointer sufficiently to achieve security impact, but we are proceeding as though that is possible.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL dict_int reads beyond zero-length tokens
advisories.summary: Buffer over-read in PostgreSQL dict_int allows a database user to disclose portions of server memory, via a zero-length token.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL plperl prepared-query use-after-free executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Use after free in PostgreSQL plperl allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via re-entering plperl and freeing a prepared query while an outer invocation is executing it.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL composite-type change during field assignment executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Type confusion in PostgreSQL composite-value field assignment allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via changing a composite type between deforming and reforming a value.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL parallel RECORD typmod use-after-free executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Use after free in PostgreSQL coordination of anonymous RECORD type identifiers among parallel workers allows a database user to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via causing one process to free a shared tuple descriptor while another process retains and later uses its address.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL foreign key and JSON conversions bypass EXECUTE privilege on cast functions
advisories.summary: Missing authorization in PostgreSQL type conversion allows a database user to invoke a cast function despite lacking EXECUTE privilege on that function, via foreign keys, to_json(), and others.  A successful attack requires the attacker to search each database for access-restricted cast functions and identify confidentiality impact specific to each function implementation found.  There are few or no practical examples of an access-restricted cast function or of a cast function having confidentiality impact.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL refint plan cache type confusion executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Type confusion in PostgreSQL module "refint" allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database.  The fix for this emerged as a non-security bug report, and the fix appear in the git repository with subject "refint: Remove plan cache.", without a CVE number.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL logical decoding can dlopen arbitrary file
advisories.summary: Missing authorization in PostgreSQL logical decoding allows a non-superuser holding REPLICATION privilege to dlopen any file visible to the operating system account running the server, via the choice of logical decoding plugin.  This in turn runs arbitrary code as that account.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL fails to check type USAGE privilege
advisories.summary: Missing authorization in PostgreSQL DDL commands allows an object creator to achieve denial of service against ALTER and DROP of the type, via creating a dependency on the type.  Many DDL operations did check the privilege, but assigning a range subtype and referencing the type from an SQL expression did not.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL ALTER TABLE ALTER TYPE resets extended statistics ownership
advisories.summary: Incorrect ownership assignment in PostgreSQL ALTER TABLE ALTER TYPE command reassigns ownership of dependent statistics objects to the current user.  This wrongly allows the table owner to run DROP STATISTICS and ALTER STATISTICS via this improper ownership.  It wrongly denies those commands to the prior statistics object owner.  DROP TABLE remains able to remove statistics objects, so this exploit achieves nothing in many ownership arrangements.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL psql COPY FROM STDIN early failure processes data lines as psql commands
advisories.summary: Untrusted data inclusion in PostgreSQL psql COPY may allow a server administrator to elicit execution of data lines as psql commands, via error injection.  If the "COPY FROM STDIN" or "\copy FROM STDIN" command fails before the server indicates that it awaits input rows, psql processes the in-line data rows as psql commands.  "COPY FROM" with a filename is unaffected.  The server administrator has no inherent control over the data rows, so a complete attack requires the attacker to separately acquire control of both the server and the data rows.  Alternatively, an attacker controlling data rows alone might complete an attack through a coincidental error that they don't control.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL pg_dump heap buffer overflow executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Heap buffer overflow in PostgreSQL pg_dump of long function transform lists allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running pg_dump, via a crafted transform list.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL psql \unrestrict lets superuser of pg_dump origin server execute arbitrary code in psql client
advisories.summary: Untrusted data inclusion in pg_dump in PostgreSQL allows a malicious superuser of the origin server to inject arbitrary code for restore-time execution as the client operating system account running psql to restore the dump, via psql \restrict meta-command input expansion.  The fix for CVE-2025-8714 introduced \restrict and \unrestrict to block this attack, but \unrestrict itself was sufficient for an attack.  pg_dumpall is also affected.  pg_restore is affected when used to generate a plain-format dump.  Non-core use of \restrict would be affected, but we've not identified non-core use.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL ascii() function reads past end of buffer
advisories.summary: Buffer over-read in PostgreSQL ascii() SQL function allows a user to disclose up to 3 bytes after the end of a specific allocation, via a crafted text value.  This is the same class of defect that CVE-2026-2006 fixed, though this instance has less impact.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL ECPG integer underflow can crash the client
advisories.summary: Integer underflow in PostgreSQL ECPG allows a database server administrator to achieve temporary denial of service against the ECPG client via sending a bytea value lacking the mandatory prefix.  The client overwrites a huge memory region with bytes outside attacker knowledge or control.  This typically yields a simple SIGSEGV, but rare cases might achieve client-specific integrity impact via the write.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL type confusion in cursor CLOSE + DECLARE executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Type confusion in PostgreSQL "portal"/cursor lifecycle allows a user to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via re-creation of a cursor or other portal with different types.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL type confusion in pg_restore_attribute_stats() executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Type confusion in PostgreSQL pg_restore_attribute_stats() allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via conflation of range and multirange values.  Within major version 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.6 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL fuzzystrmatch writes effectively-arbitrary addresses, via integer wraparound
advisories.summary: Integer wraparound in PostgreSQL fuzzystrmatch allows a user to direct writes to a huge range of addresses, executing arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via extreme inputs to SQL function levenshtein() or levenshtein_less_equal().  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL expression deparse allows SQL injection via EXTRACT argument
advisories.summary: SQL injection in PostgreSQL EXTRACT() deparse allows an object owner to execute arbitrary SQL as a superuser via a hostile object definition.  Attacks affect expression deparse consumers broadly, including pg_dump, psql commands like \sf, and any similar usage in non-core tools.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL improper enforcement of GSSAPI encryption when coupled with SSL
advisories.summary: Improper enforcement of message integrity in PostgreSQL GSSAPI support allows a user to negotiate GSSAPI contrary to pg_hba.conf rules, via initial direct TLS connection.  Despite a pg_hba.conf that appears to require GSSAPI, the connection may exchange data over TLS encryption alone.  If the TLS settings are more permissive than the GSS settings, the connection may continue with lesser protection.  Within major versions 17-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.6 and 17.11 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 17 are unaffected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL type confusion via "internal" arguments
advisories.summary: Type confusion with PostgreSQL "internal" data type arguments allows any user to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via calls to functions with that argument type.  Type "internal" represents a class of mutually-incompatible data structures not intended for access from SQL.  The system intended to prevent such function calls, but this prevention had gaps.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL stack buffer overflow in argument match writes 0x0 and 0x1 to server memory
advisories.summary: Stack buffer overflow in PostgreSQL argument name matching allows an object creator to achieve unknown impacts via OUT parameter count.  The attack can write only 0x0 and 0x1 bytes.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL pg_trgm picksplit reads past end of buffer
advisories.summary: Buffer over-read in PostgreSQL pg_trgm index picksplit function reads past end of a heap buffer.  This might allow a table maintainer to infer limited memory values, via the lossy signal of index split choices.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL 32-bit pltcl and plperl undersize allocations, via integer wraparound
advisories.summary: Integer wraparound in PostgreSQL 32-bit builds of pltcl and plperl allows an object creator to cause the server to undersize an allocation and write out-of-bounds via crafted function bodies.  This may execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database.  CVE-2026-6473 had fixed similar problems.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL pg_stat_statements heap buffer overflow executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Heap buffer overflow in PostgreSQL pg_stat_statements allows the query author to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via crafted queries containing array constants.  Within major version 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.6 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL amcheck does not clear untrusted search path
advisories.summary: Untrusted search path in PostgreSQL amcheck allows a grantee of amcheck function EXECUTE privilege to execute arbitrary functions as the owners of expression indexes that depend on the search path, via setting a hostile search path before calling the amcheck function.  Within major versions 18, 16, 15, and 14, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.  PostgreSQL 17 is unaffected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL observable response discrepancy with non-default scram_iterations provides user existence oracle
advisories.summary: Observable response discrepancy in PostgreSQL SCRAM authentication allows an unauthenticated user to test the existence of a user via observing the SCRAM iteration count.  This requires the probed user to have a non-default scram_iterations count, because the authentication challenge for a nonexistent user reports the default scram_iterations.  Within major versions 16-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, and 16.15 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 16 are unaffected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL plperl tied object heap buffer overflow executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Heap buffer overflow in PostgreSQL plperl return of a tied hash allows the function owner to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via a crafted function body.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL to_char heap buffer overflow executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Heap buffer overflow in PostgreSQL to_char(timestamptz) allows the party choosing the timezone to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via a long POSIX timezone abbreviation.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL ctid type confusion in selectivity estimator discloses derivative of arbitrary read
advisories.summary: Type confusion regarding input of PostgreSQL ctid data type selectivity estimator allows an object creator to view a calculation derived from the value of an arbitrary 4-byte span of memory, via a chosen non-ctid input.  While the calculation loses precision, substantial memory value recovery appears possible.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL row security caching disregards role modifications
advisories.summary: Incomplete tracking in PostgreSQL of changes to role membership, role attributes, and database ownership allows a query to continue using cached row-level security policies after those changes require a different policy, via plan reuse.  Stale policies continue until some other event invalidates the cache or connection termination ends the session.  This permits a user to complete reads and modifications that were recently permitted but now forbidden.  An attacker must tailor an attack to a particular application's pattern of privilege removal and role-specific row security policies.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL regexp heap buffer overflow executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Heap buffer overflow in PostgreSQL regexp allows the query author to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via text that would not pass encoding validation.  This shares heritage with CVE-2026-2006, but this case involved unanticipated data growth when round-tripped through pg_wchar.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL pgcrypto, for OpenSSL-disabled ciphers, silently encrypts to and decrypts from cleartext
advisories.summary: Cleartext storage in PostgreSQL pgcrypto disabled ciphers allows a user to recover cleartext, via direct observation of the faulty ciphertext.  The OpenSSL version and OpenSSL configuration determine the disabled ciphers.  If the application accepts encrypted data as input, decryption will succeed even with the wrong key.  This in turn loses the modest protection from the Modification Detection Code (MDC).  Affected functions are pgp_sym_encrypt, pgp_sym_decrypt, pgp_pub_encrypt, pgp_pub_decrypt, pgp_sym_encrypt_bytea, pgp_sym_decrypt_bytea, pgp_pub_encrypt_bytea, and pgp_pub_decrypt_bytea.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL tsvector and tsquery undersize allocations, via integer wraparound
advisories.summary: Integer wraparound in PostgreSQL tsvector and tsquery data type functions allows an unprivileged database user to cause the server to undersize an allocation and write out-of-bounds, via crafted large inputs.  This may execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database.  These types are typically sourced from application logic, not taken from the application's user.  Hence, application users attacking the database, through the application as a conduit, are unlikely.  CVE-2026-6473 had fixed similar problems.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL REFRESH PUBLICATION allows SQL injection via table name
advisories.summary: SQL injection in PostgreSQL logical replication ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH PUBLICATION allows a subscriber table creator to execute arbitrary SQL with the subscription's publication-side credentials.  The attack takes effect at the next REFRESH PUBLICATION.  Within major versions 16, 17, and 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.4, 17.10, and 16.14 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 16 are unaffected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL refint allows stack buffer overflow and SQL injection
advisories.summary: Stack buffer overflow in PostgreSQL module "refint" allows an unprivileged database user to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database.  A distinct attack is possible if the application declares a user-controlled column as a "refint" cascade primary key and facilitates user-controlled updates to that column.  In that case, a SQL injection allows a primary key update value provider to execute arbitrary SQL as the database user performing the primary key update.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.4, 17.10, 16.14, 15.18, and 14.23 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL pg_restore_attribute_stats accepts values that cause query planning to read past end of stats array
advisories.summary: Buffer over-read in PostgreSQL function pg_restore_attribute_stats() accepts array values of unmatched length, which causes query planning to read past end of one array.  This allows a table maintainer to infer memory values past that array end.  Within major version 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.4 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL SSL/GSS init causes denial of service, via uncontrolled recursion
advisories.summary: Uncontrolled recursion in PostgreSQL SSL and GSS negotiation allows an attacker able to connect to a PostgreSQL AF_UNIX socket to achieve sustained denial of service.  If SSL and GSS are both disabled, an attacker can do the same via access to a PostgreSQL TCP socket.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.4, 17.10, 16.14, 15.18, and 14.23 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL discloses MD5-hashed passwords via covert timing channel
advisories.summary: Covert timing channel in comparison of MD5-hashed password in PostgreSQL authentication allows an attacker to recover user credentials sufficient to authenticate.  This does not affect scram-sha-256 passwords, the default in all supported releases.  However, current databases may have MD5-hashed passwords originating in upgrades from PostgreSQL 13 or earlier.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.4, 17.10, 16.14, 15.18, and 14.23 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL libpq lo_* functions let server superuser overwrite client stack memory
advisories.summary: Use of inherently dangerous function PQfn(..., result_is_int=0, ...) in PostgreSQL libpq lo_export(), lo_read(), lo_lseek64(), and lo_tell64() functions allows the server superuser to overwrite a client stack buffer with an arbitrarily-large response.  Like gets(), PQfn(..., result_is_int=0, ...) stores arbitrary-length, server-determined data into a buffer of unspecified size.  Because both the \lo_export command in psql and pg_dump call lo_read(), the server superuser can overwrite pg_dump or psql stack memory.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.4, 17.10, 16.14, 15.18, and 14.23 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL pg_createsubscriber allows SQL injection via subscription name
advisories.summary: SQL injection in PostgreSQL pg_createsubscriber allows an attacker with pg_create_subscription rights to execute arbitrary SQL as a superuser.  The attack takes effect when pg_createsubscriber next runs.  Within major versions 17 and 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.4 and 17.10 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 17 are unaffected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL pg_basebackup and pg_rewind can overwrite unrelated files of origin superuser choice
advisories.summary: Symlink following in PostgreSQL pg_basebackup plain format and in pg_rewind allows an origin superuser to overwrite local files, e.g. /var/lib/postgres/.bashrc, that hijack the operating system account.  It will remain the case that starting the server after these commands implicitly trusts the origin superuser, due to features like shared_preload_libraries.  Hence, the attack has practical implications only if one takes relevant action between these commands and server start, like moving the files to a different VM or snapshotting the VM.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.4, 17.10, 16.14, 15.18, and 14.23 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL timeofday() can disclose portions of server memory
advisories.summary: Externally-controlled format string in PostgreSQL timeofday() function allows an attacker to retrieve portions of server memory, via crafted timezone zones.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.4, 17.10, 16.14, 15.18, and 14.23 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL server undersizes allocations, via integer wraparound
advisories.summary: Integer wraparound in multiple PostgreSQL server features allows an unprivileged database user to cause the server to undersize an allocation and write out-of-bounds.  This may execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database.  In applications that pass gigabyte-scale user inputs to the relevant database functions, the application input provider may achieve a segmentation fault.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.4, 17.10, 16.14, 15.18, and 14.23 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL CREATE TYPE does not check multirange schema CREATE privilege
advisories.summary: Missing authorization in PostgreSQL CREATE TYPE allows an object creator to hijack other queries that use search_path to find user-defined types, including extension-defined types.  That is to say, the victim will execute arbitrary SQL functions of the attacker's choice.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.4, 17.10, 16.14, 15.18, and 14.23 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL pg_trgm heap buffer overflow writes pattern onto server memory
advisories.summary: Heap buffer overflow in PostgreSQL pg_trgm allows a database user to achieve unknown impacts via a crafted input string.  The attacker has limited control over the byte patterns to be written, but we have not ruled out the viability of attacks that lead to privilege escalation.  PostgreSQL 18.1 and 18.0 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL missing validation of multibyte character length executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Missing validation of multibyte character length in PostgreSQL text manipulation allows a database user to issue crafted queries that achieve a buffer overrun.  That suffices to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.2, 17.8, 16.12, 15.16, and 14.21 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL pgcrypto heap buffer overflow executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Heap buffer overflow in PostgreSQL pgcrypto allows a ciphertext provider to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.2, 17.8, 16.12, 15.16, and 14.21 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL intarray missing validation of type of input to selectivity estimator executes arbitrary code
advisories.summary: Missing validation of type of input in PostgreSQL intarray extension selectivity estimator function allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.2, 17.8, 16.12, 15.16, and 14.21 are affected.

advisories.title: PostgreSQL oidvector discloses a few bytes of memory
advisories.summary: Improper validation of type "oidvector" in PostgreSQL allows a database user to disclose a few bytes of server memory.  We have not ruled out viability of attacks that arrange for presence of confidential information in disclosed bytes, but they seem unlikely.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.2, 17.8, 16.12, 15.16, and 14.21 are affected.
